title: Lesson 42 - Generative AI Grounded on Data 360: RAG, Prompts, and the Trust Layer
description: Apply predictive and generative AI tooling capabilities of Data 360 to customer scenarios, focusing on retrieval and grounding, prompt and agent use cases, the trust layer, and the governance a customer expects before AI touches unified customer data.

questions.question: A team wants an agent to answer questions from internal documents and from customer data in Data 360. What must be configured for the documents to be retrieved?
options: Nothing, because the language model already knows the documents
Connect the content and create a search index that chunks and vectorizes it
Add the documents as CRM record fields only
Disable the Einstein Trust Layer for retrieval
questions.explanation: Retrieval augmented generation pulls context from a search index, so the content must be connected and indexed into chunked, vectorized data before an agent can retrieve it. The model does not already know your documents, record fields alone do not index them, and the trust layer is not disabled for retrieval.

questions.question: Which statement about the Einstein Trust Layer is TRUE?
options: Grounding data is retrieved regardless of the user's permissions
Prompts are grounded only with data the executing user can access, and prompts, responses, and trust signals are logged as an audit trail in Data 360
Customer data is used to train the language model
Toxicity scoring replaces the need for permissions
questions.explanation: Secure data retrieval grounds the prompt only with data the executing user can access, preserving role based controls and field level security, and the layer logs prompts, responses, and trust signals as an audit trail stored in Data 360. Customer data is not used to train the model, and toxicity scoring does not replace access controls.

questions.question: A prompt must include a value computed by an Apex process and an attribute from a Data 360 data model object. Which approach fits?
options: Grounding with merge fields, which can source record fields, flow or Apex values, and Data 360 data model objects
Hard coding the values into the prompt text
Using CRM record fields only, because Data 360 objects cannot be used
Vectorizing the values before every prompt
questions.explanation: Prompt Builder grounds with merge fields, and those fields can source CRM record fields, values produced by a flow or Apex, Data 360 data model objects, and related lists. Hard coding is not grounding, Data 360 objects are supported, and vectorizing is part of building the search index, not something done per prompt run.
